Use [`gmeow:transactionHash`](gmeow-transactionHash.md) from [`gmeow:LedgerTransaction`](../classes/gmeow-LedgerTransaction.md) to [`rdfs:Literal`](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Literal) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Common Companion Terms

[`gmeow:LedgerTransaction`](../classes/gmeow-LedgerTransaction.md)

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to carry the hash that identifies a [`gmeow:LedgerTransaction`](../classes/gmeow-LedgerTransaction.md) on its chain — the stable on-chain identity used to look up and re-verify the transaction.

### Avoid when

- Avoid for a block's hash ([`gmeow:blockHash`](gmeow-blockHash.md)) or a chain identifier ([`gmeow:chainId`](gmeow-chainId.md)); the transaction hash identifies one transaction, not its block or its network. Functional — one hash per transaction.

### How to use

- Set one transaction-hash literal on the [`gmeow:LedgerTransaction`](../classes/gmeow-LedgerTransaction.md); pair it with the containing [`gmeow:Block`](../classes/gmeow-Block.md) and [`gmeow:BlockchainNetwork`](../classes/gmeow-BlockchainNetwork.md) so the hash resolves unambiguously.

### Examples

- ex:tx1 [`gmeow:transactionHash`](gmeow-transactionHash.md) "0xabc123...".
